messages:
maria: Quick ping — PR #2345 updates quantization + prefix caching for gpt-medium serving. Can someone eyeball perf/cost changes? Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/2345 :eyes:

ci-bot: CI started for 2345 (commit abc123)...

leo: I'll take a look in ~30m. Did you run the microbench against 4k and 64k seq lengths?

maria: Yep — results in the PR description. TL;DR: int8 quant + prefix cache -> ~2.3x token cost reduction on our sample workload, p50 latency up ~12ms on avg. Full numbers: p50 78ms -> 90ms, throughput up 2.1x. Artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/perf/2345/

ash: Any change to smart routing? If the quantized variant OOMs we should auto-fallback to fp16.

maria: No routing changes. I added a runtime compatibility check: if model init fails due to OOM or kernel mismatch we fall back to the fp16 variant and emit a metric (in PR code comment).

jamie: Heads up — eng-runtime CI showing kv_cache tests failing on linux-ubuntu matrix. Stack snippet:
```
ERROR: AssertionError: expected cache size 128 != 0
Traceback (most recent call last)...
```

maria: I saw that. Repro locally with `docker-compose -f infra/test/docker-compose.yml run test_ubuntu pytest -k kv_cache` — pushing a small fix patch in ~45m.

erin: Tagging @leo — we'll gate rollout on your review + green canary. Suggest canary 10% dedicated for 24h, then 50%.

leo: Ack. I'll focus on perf assumptions and the new compatibility check. If the kv_cache fix is small I can re-review quickly. Also suggest splitting the big `load_model()` into init + warmup to reduce try/catch complexity.

ash: If timeline is tight I can approve after tests pass and a short QA run. :+1:

maria: Thanks — will follow up. Plan: push test fix, re-run CI, re-upload microbench logs, request formal review from @leo. If green then canary as Erin suggested.

ci-bot: CI finished: build passed (2345, commit abc123) :white_check_mark:

leo: Reviewing now — should have comments in ~20m. :mag:

maria: Appreciate it — will address quickly. :rocket:
